Abstract 
Stiff-person syndrome (SPS) is a rare disorder of the nervous system, characterized by muscle stiffness, rigidity, 
and painful spasms involving truncal and limb musculature that may severely limit mobility.  
Our case documents a 53 -year-old patient with SPS and endometrial cancer who was pos itive for anti-GAD 
and paraneoplastic antibodies, who presented to our institution for robotic surgery. These patients are at high 
risk for prolonged hypotonia and mechanical ventilation. Our patient underwent general anesthesia without 
complications despite multiple comorbidities.
